profile.status: Out of service, replaced by M14

through_line: The M1 Garand's design idea of a gas-operated, semi-automatic rifle with a rotating bolt and en-bloc clip feeding system survived every revision.

stages.title: Initial Design
stages.summary: John Garand developed the first prototype of the M1 Garand, utilizing a primer-actuated system. The design was mechanically efficient, with parts organized into compact, self-contained units.
stages.impact: Led to further development and refinement of the design

stages.title: Refined Prototype
stages.summary: Garand refined his design, creating the M1924 prototype, which was sent to U.S. infantry and cavalry units for field trials. The M1924 used a primer-actuated blowback system.
stages.driver: Need for a more reliable and efficient design
stages.impact: Led to the development of the T1E1 prototype

stages.title: Gas-Operated Prototype
stages.summary: The T1E1 prototype was developed, featuring a gas-operated system. The T1E1 was manufactured at Springfield Armory and underwent testing.
stages.driver: Need for a more reliable and efficient design
stages.impact: Led to the adoption of the M1 Garand

stages.title: Standard-Issue Rifle
stages.summary: The M1 Garand was adopted as the standard-issue rifle for the U.S. military, replacing the M1903 Springfield. The M1 Garand used a gas-operated, closed rotating bolt system.
stages.driver: Need for a semi-automatic rifle for military use
stages.impact: Became the primary rifle for the U.S. military during World War II and the Korean War

changes.detail: from a gas trap to a drilled gas port

stages.title: Sniper Variant
stages.summary: The M1C sniper variant was developed, featuring a scope mount attached to the receiver. However, the procedure for installing the mounts reduced accuracy.
stages.impact: Led to the development of the M1D variant

stages.title: Improved Sniper Variant
stages.summary: The M1D variant was developed, featuring a mount attached to the barrel instead of the receiver, improving accuracy.
stages.driver: Need for a more accurate sniper variant
stages.impact: Became the standard sniper rifle for the U.S. military

stages.title: Final Form
stages.summary: The M1 Garand was replaced by the M14 rifle, marking the end of its service life. However, the M1 Garand remains popular among collectors and civilian shooters.
stages.driver: Need for a more modern and selective-fire rifle
stages.impact: Led to the development of new rifles, such as the M14 and M16
